chapter: Piano influences: Teddy Wilson, Tatum and Bud Powell
title: Trummy's replacements Swindell and Ike Quebec; Clyde Hart's piano lessons
summary: After Chicago and the Yacht Club, Leo Williams and Harry Curtis leave and are replaced; Clyde Hart shows him piano ideas.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Anyway, he did the engagement with us in Chicago, and after Chicago we went to New York in the Yacht Club, and I think Leo was with us for a short while. But for some reason, Leo left the band, and the alto saxophone player, Harry Curtis, got drafted into the Navy. So we got another kid who had grown up in Washington but was living in Baltimore at that particular time, and his name was William Swindell. We got him to play alto saxophone in Harry Curtis's place. A

And in Leo Williams's place on tenor saxophone we got a fellow who lived in Newark, New Jersey, and his name was Ike Quebec, which we became very good friends later. Ike was an excellent tenor saxophone player, plus he also played the piano. So that gave us a bond right there. I was trying to write then, and he would give me different suggestions about different things. For a guy his age... Because Ike was around

the same age as myself, I think, but living in New York, or in Newark, New Jersey, which you always think of as New York, because Newark, New Jersey musicians were always in New York... It's just faster up there and guys learn much faster.

Anyway, I want to kind of backtrack and mention these people. And I think I mentioned Clyde Hart, when I was talking about the band that worked with us at the Yacht Club when I was there with Trummy Young. I mentioned Clyde Hart working with Coleman Hawkins and Dizzy Gillespie, Oscar Pettiford and Jackie Miles.

Anyway, Clyde Hart did a lot... He showed me a lot of things about playing the piano. Clyde was quite a busy musician then. He was making a lot of record dates and doing a lot of writing, and he was very much in demand. Unfortunately, he died not long after that. I think it was around this time when... I don't know whether it was at that particular time, or whether... I think it was probably later. Because a couple of years later, after I had worked in that Eckstine band, I did go back to 52nd Street, and I played there with any number of people, including Billy Eckstine and Billie Holiday...
